# Supporting-cap directional inverses and buffered contact continuation

This note removes the regular-cap derivative hypothesis from the finite
buffered contact-minimum continuation, for the same class of actual
bounded signed radial first-speed paths. Proper OWN sections remain
essential. Positive-area supporting OTHER-fiber traces are kept exactly
through their max/min responses; no C1 assertion or free allocation is
made.

The exact covering construction is
`candidate c6bafe9ff5de0861`,
Sections 1--2. Its energy/covariance contact derivative is unchanged.
Only its regular quantile differentiation is replaced here.

Independent full audit: `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`,
PASS. The source checker `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_supporting_cap_directional_inverses_slab_recovery.py`
passes 197 exact checks, including 168 ACTUAL affine-parallelogram
clippings across all cap statuses with nonconstant signed facet speeds.
The independent interval/branch checker passes 1,218 exact checks.
These are calibrations of the analytic proof, not its replacement.

## 1. Actual path and the all-status scalar cap response

Fix positive convex fibers K_z on a finite base P. The actual compatible
path K_z(t) satisfies the signed radial hypotheses of Section 3 of the
preceding source: a common interior origin in each fiber, radial
displacements bounded in absolute value by Ct, and bounded signed
INWARD normal first speed v_z almost everywhere. The path may add and
remove volume. Let

    H={a.z+u.X>=c},    u!=0,    b=||u||,
    s_z=c-a.z.

Classify the old fiber cuts as strict full, inside supporting, proper,
outside supporting, or strict empty, according as s_z lies below the
minimum of u.X, equals that minimum, lies strictly between its extrema,
equals its maximum, or lies above the maximum. An inside supporting
closed cap contains its WHOLE fiber; an outside supporting closed cap
has zero d-volume. Put F_z=K_z intersect {u.X=s_z} on a supporting
fiber and D_z=integral_(boundary K_z) v_z dS.

Define

    B_H(v)=sum_(strict full or inside) D_z
             +sum_(proper) integral_(boundary K_z)
                                      1_{u.X>=s_z} v_z dS,

    S_H^proper=sum_(proper)
                       H^(d-1)(K_z intersect {u.X=s_z})/b.

The exact scalar first LOSS response to a threshold increase t r is

    R_H(r)=B_H(v)+S_H^proper r
          +sum_(inside) integral_(F_z) (r/b-v_z)_+ dS
          -sum_(outside) integral_(F_z) (-r/b-v_z)_+ dS.          (1)

For every bounded interval of r values,

    mu_t{a.z+u.X>=c+t r}
               =mu_0(H)-t R_H(r)+o(t)                          (2)

uniformly on that interval. All facets here are old physical supporting
faces and all terms use the SAME actual path.

In particular R_H(0) is the actual fixed CLOSED-cap loss. At supporting
fibers it need not equal integral 1_H v on the old boundary. Outward
movement on an inside supporting facet is clipped by the old cap,
whereas outward movement on an outside supporting facet can add
captured volume.

## 2. Proof of the supporting-facet expansion

The strict full/empty cases are stable for bounded r. For a proper
cut, old threshold coarea gives the term S_z r. The radial shell term
gives integral 1_H v: the cut plane has zero old boundary surface
measure. Uniformity follows by discarding a shrinking boundary collar
of that plane, whose surface measure tends to zero, and applying the
bounded radial expansion on its complement. Interior convex-body
section area is continuous at the proper threshold, including the
constant d=1 case.

For completeness consider an OUTSIDE supporting fiber. Choose its
fixed radial origin o in int K_z. At almost every X in its supporting
face the outward normal is n=u/b and

    H_o=n.(X-o)>0,   u.(X-o)=b H_o.

Use the relative inward radial coordinate r_rad, so a point on this
ray is o+(1-r_rad)(X-o). The new body's endpoint has coordinate
s_t(X), where |s_t|<=Ct and H_o s_t/t->v_z in L1 on the boundary.
The shifted cap condition on this ray is exactly

    r_rad <= -t r/(b H_o).

Thus its newly captured radial segment has first-order length
[-t r/(b H_o)-s_t]_+. The radial volume Jacobian at the old endpoint
is H_o dS, so its first volume is

    t integral_(F_z) (-r/b-v_z)_+ dS.

This is a GAIN, hence the negative sign in (1). Rays ending away from
F_z have a fixed strict gap and eventually contribute zero. Rays in
a shrinking nonfacet collar have uniformly O(t) contribution and
vanishing boundary measure. Inner-ball bounds control the radial
denominators on that collar. This proves the limit by dominated
convergence. The positive-part Lipschitz inequality and the L1 radial
speed convergence make it uniform for bounded r.

At an INSIDE supporting fiber, n=-u/b on F_z and
u.(X-o)=-b H_o. The cap condition becomes

    r_rad >= t r/(b H_o).

The actual radial boundary of the captured body is therefore the
larger of s_t and t r/(b H_o). Its first loss on that face is

    integral_(F_z) max(v_z,r/b) dS.

On all other old boundary points its first loss is v_z. Hence the
total is D_z+integral_(F_z)(r/b-v_z)_+, exactly the inside term in
(1). The same bounded-collar argument proves uniformity. Negative
values are allowed: if the path expands and the threshold moves
outward sufficiently, this loss is negative.

Supporting faces with zero (d-1)-measure contribute zero to these
formulas. In d=1 use the two boundary endpoints with H^0 measure; the
same clipped radial interval computation is exact. Nonsmooth joins of
a positive-area facet have zero facet-boundary measure and cause no
additional first-order term.

## 3. Strict scalar invertibility comes from the own proper trace

Assume H has a proper cut in at least one positive fiber, as every
selected buffered cap does at its assigned source. Then
S_H^proper>0. Every hinge contribution in (1) is nondecreasing in r,
including the negative outside hinge. For r_2>r_1,

    S_H^proper (r_2-r_1)
       <=R_H(r_2)-R_H(r_1)
       <=S_H^all (r_2-r_1),                                    (3)

where

    S_H^all=S_H^proper+sum_(supporting) H^(d-1)(F_z)/b.

Thus R_H is continuous, strictly increasing, and maps R onto R. It
has a globally Lipschitz inverse, even when a supporting branch has
a corner or a whole tie region. It need not be affine or differentiable.

## 4. Exact nonsmooth common-mass quantile continuation

Fix one old buffered witness group H_j with positive rho_j summing
to one and common old mass Q. Let alpha(t) be its exact full-contact
budget from the invariant continuation source, including the updated
norm and mass; assume its proved expansion

    alpha(t)=t alpha'+o(t),    alpha(0)=0.

The current common mass q(t) is still defined by the EXACT scalar
quantile equation

    sum_j rho_j c_j(t,q(t))=sum_j rho_j c_j(0,Q)+alpha(t).        (4)

Its actual covering interpretation and off-old-base strict gaps are
unchanged. No regularity of the selected cap masses is required to
define it.

Let R_j be (1) for the j-th fixed normal and the actual speed array.
Then q has the exact right derivative

    q'(0+)=-ell,
    sum_j rho_j R_j^(-1)(ell)=alpha'.                           (5)

There is a UNIQUE ell solving (5), by (3). To prove it, first use the
bounded radial volume change and the uniformly positive proper own
section to obtain q(t)-Q=O(t) and
c_j(t,q(t))-c_j(0,Q)=O(t). Equivalently this follows by bracketing
q=Q plus or minus a sufficiently large constant times t in (4),
using (2)--(3). Set

    ell_t=(Q-q(t))/t,
    r_jt=[c_j(t,q(t))-c_j(0,Q)]/t.

These are bounded. The uniform expansion (2) gives
ell_t=R_j(r_jt)+o(1), and (3) permits inversion:

    r_jt=R_j^(-1)(ell_t)+o(1).

Dividing (4) by t proves (5) for every subsequential limit. Uniqueness
then proves convergence of ell_t itself. This is an actual directional
quantile derivative, not a postulated generalized gradient.

Let D be the total signed inward volume loss, and beta=Q/M. Strict
normalized decrease for this covering group is equivalent to ell>beta D.
Since the left side of (5) is strictly increasing, the exact criterion
is

    sum_j rho_j R_j^(-1)(beta D) < alpha'.                       (6)

For finitely many groups, if the SAME actual path satisfies (6) in
every group, the maximum normalized buffered depth strictly decreases.
Conversely an attained minimum forbids that simultaneous strict
criterion. This is the precise nonsmooth payment obligation; no
assertion that it always holds is made.

## 5. Allocations are recovered, not freely prescribed

At the uniquely determined shifts r_j=R_j^(-1)(ell), each inside
facet permits a selector sigma in [0,1] with

    sigma=1 where r_j/b>v,   sigma=0 where r_j/b<v,

so max(v,r_j/b)=(1-sigma)v+sigma r_j/b. Each outside facet permits
a selector tau with

    tau=1 where v+r_j/b<0,   tau=0 where v+r_j/b>0,

so its loss min(v+r_j/b,0)=tau v+tau r_j/b. Ties permit any selector
in [0,1]; every choice gives the same scalar loss at that shift.

Consequently R_j(r_j)=L_j^alloc+S_j^alloc r_j, with

    S_j^alloc=S_j^proper
          +sum_inside integral sigma/b +sum_outside integral tau/b,

and L_j^alloc equal to proper/strict-full losses, inside facet body
weights 1-sigma, and outside facet body weights tau. In particular
its explicit formula is

    L_j^alloc=B_(H_j)(v)-sum_inside integral sigma v
                               +sum_outside integral tau v.

Thus the other boundary of each inside fiber keeps its full body
loss. In particular
S_j^alloc>=S_j^proper>0. Substituting these CONSISTENT allocations in
(5) recovers the harmonic-weight expression

    ell=sum_j theta_j L_j^alloc
                      +alpha'/sum_j(rho_j/S_j^alloc),
    theta_j=(rho_j/S_j^alloc)/sum_l(rho_l/S_l^alloc).

This is an identity after the threshold solution. It does not authorize
choosing body allocations and section allocations independently, or
optimizing each supporting cap separately. Formula (5) is independent
of all tie choices and is the unambiguous formulation.

## 6. Exact supporting interval calibration

Take three identical interval fibers [-1,1] at bases -1,0,1. Fix
0<delta<1 and the cap

    (1+delta)z+X >= -delta.

Its original mass is Q=3+delta. Its positive endpoint fiber is strict
full, its middle cut is proper, and its negative endpoint fiber is
OUTSIDE supporting at X=1. Under the actual homothetic path
K_z(t)=[-1+h t,1-h t], with signed constant inward speed h, an additional
threshold increase t r gives exactly, for small t,

    captured mass=3+delta-t(3h+r)+t(-h-r)_+.

Therefore

    R(r)=3h+r-(-h-r)_+,

with slopes two below -h and one above -h. This agrees with (1).
An outward path h<0 at a fixed threshold has a nonzero gain from the
supporting endpoint that a C1 proper-only formula would omit. The
inverse criterion retains this contribution automatically.

This calibration is not the general theorem's proof; that proof is
the all-dimensional supporting-facet radial calculation above.
